nodes.text: Bank of Silverfall. Four vaults, one ledger, no exceptions. State your business — in figures, where possible.

choices.text: You charter the ford bank, I hear.
Has the open seal changed your business?

nodes.text: Deposit at any bank chest; withdraw at any other. Your holdings live in the ledger, not the box, which means brigands can steal a *box* and acquire nothing but the box. The vault row behind me is the ledger's teeth. Nothing in twenty years has gotten past it, including, on one memorable audit, me.

Cormund of Amberford. Twelve pages a season, each one requiring a single line of reply. He frames the correspondence as professional necessity; I diagnose enthusiasm. His vault-work is nonetheless immaculate, and his Toll War chain hangs in his own vault as institutional memory. Sentiment, filed correctly, is indistinguishable from rigor.

Materially. Deep Market silver moves through my counters now, the ore brokers below bank their take up here nightly, and I have opened a fifth column in a ledger that had not needed one since my predecessor's predecessor. Growth is turbulence that pays for itself. We are watching it with both eyes.
